newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds mixed, await top-tier data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds mixed, await top-tier data.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were mixed and spreads to Treasuries remained largely unchanged in late trade on Thursday.
Most market participants were sidelined, waiting for economic data to surface and offer the market some direction, traders said.

"Things right now are very quiet," one pass-through trader said. "We're just waiting for some news to stir things up in one direction or another," he said, referring to Friday's reports on producer prices and retail sales for March.
By 1535 EDT/1635 GMT, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent paper was off 1/32 at 100-23/32 bid, yielding 112 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were up 1/32 at 100-26/32 bid, while Freddie Mac paper was unchanged at 101 even.
The five-year Treasury note was down 2/32 at 99-12/32 bid to yield 6.77 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was off 2/32, yielding 6.91 percent.

Looking forward, Treasury prices are likely to stick to their current range, said BZW Securities Inc mortgage analyst Cynthia Rivera. She said that if Friday's economic data do not deviate from market expectations, her outlook for pass-throughs will remain neutral.
"The focus next week will probably be on the (dollar) roll," she said.
Economists in a Reuters poll forecast the March headline producer price index and retail sales figures to be unchanged and 0.6 percent higher, respectively.
